newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus sees 96 sales around $20 billion.
newsitem.headline: Airbus sees 96 sales around $20 billion.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie expects to post 1996 sales of around $20 billion based on forecast orders for more than 300 aircraft, an Airbus spokesman said on Thursday.

"We will definitely top 300 planes, made up of a healthy mix of wide-body and single-aisle aircraft," he told Reuters. That mix would probably be worth about $20 billion, assuming average list prices for those product types.

As of the end of November Airbus had booked 283 firm orders, consisting of downpayments and sales contracts signed. Around 90 of those consisted of wide-body aircraft in the A330/340 family and the A300-600 plane. Average price for the A330/340 is $125 million.
The average price for the A320 family of narrow-bodies, comprising the A319, A320 and A321, is $50 million.
Airbus sold 106 planes in 1995 worth $7 billion.

Airbus Industrie is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
U.S. archrival Boeing says it has received 621 planes on order as at the end of November, of which 458 were for U.S. customers.
